overall: The AG found the Adams Board of Selectmen violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to periodically review executive session minutes; the violation was intentional due to prior advice, but no civil penalty was recommended, and a further release-timing allegation was not reviewed.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to periodically review executive session minutes to determine whether a continued purpose for nondisclosure existed.
allegations.key_passage: Here, the Board acknowledges, and we find, that it failed to review executive session minutes at reasonable intervals to determine if continued nondisclosure was warranted.

allegations.summary: On further review, complainant alleged the Board untimely released some executive session minutes and kept withholding them after disclosure was allowed; this was not in the original complaint.
allegations.key_passage: We find that this allegation was not clearly raised in the original complaint and thus we do not review its merits.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements (order to the Board).
All members of the Board must attend a webinar training on the Open Meeting Law conducted by the Attorney General's office within 100 days.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements and caution the Board that a future finding of an intentional violation of the Open Meeting Law may result in a civil penalty of up to $1,000 per violation.
